text:
incident-bot: PAGED: SolacePay (tenant t-solace-01) - elevated 5xx via NLB in eu-west-2. Pager: @oncall-sre. Metrics link: https://metrics.redwood/internal/alerts/1768012345
oncall-sre: I'm on it, moving thread to #incidents. Starting initial triage.
alice: seeing spike in 5xx from NLB listener arn:aws:...:listener/lnr-12345 -> target group tg-0a1b2c. Healthchecks failing 502/504.
ben: tagging network: @carla @dave any recent SG/NLB config changes for SolacePay?
carla: no recent SG changes from infra. Checking NLB target health now.
dave: digging into app logs in tenant VPC, nginx upstream returning 502 intermittently, but CPU/memory look normal on pods. Could be upstream cache or connection limits.
alice: quick DNS check: `dig +short t-solace-01.prod.solacepay.internal` -> `10.12.45.22
10.12.45.23` (these map to NLB nodes)
carla: ran `aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:eu-west-2:123456:targetgroup/tg-0a1b2c/abcdef` -> 8/10 targets Unhealthy (Reason: Target.ResponseCode != 200), health check failing on path `/hc`
eve: given this is a private VPC and a dedicated/tenant pool, suggestion: isolate traffic by swapping NLB listener to standby target group (tg-standby) to stop customer impact while we root-cause. Alternative is SG rule to block specific client ranges but that may be riskier.
oncall-sre: I agree with listener swap (Plan A). alice / ben can you do a controlled swap and monitor? Command (example):
```
aws elbv2 modify-listener --listener-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:eu-west-2:123456:listener/lnr-12345 --default-actions '[{"Type":"forward","TargetGroupArn":"arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:eu-west-2:123456:targetgroup/tg-standby/standbyid"}]'
```
ben: prepping a dry-run and will check Route53 TTL / traffic policies. If swap doesn't stabilize, we'll do weighted DNS shift.
alice: performing listener swap now (will monitor CloudWatch). ETA ~30s.
alice: swap executed at 1768012478, healthchecks for tg-standby returning healthy (10/10) within 45s.
incident-bot: AUTO-METRIC UPDATE: request_5xx_rate(t-solace-01) dropped from 35% -> 3% over 90s.
carla: backend still logs a few 502s but rate is much lower. Looks like the standby pool is healthy.
dave: continuing to tail app logs in tenant VPC for root cause - seeing upstream cache timeouts during peak bursts. Noting connection pool exhaustion on 10.20.0.0/24.
oncall-sre: sending customer-facing note to SolacePay: "We routed traffic to a healthy standby pool to mitigate elevated 5xx. We're investigating root cause (likely upstream cache connection exhaustion). No data lost. Will follow up in 30m with RCA."
ben: added a slow-weighted Route53 failover plan as backup (TTL 60s) in case NLB swap shows regression during scale events.
alice: creating follow-up ticket INF-4521: "t-solace-01 NLB 5xx - mitigation + RCA" with logs and timeline. Assigned to eng-ml (cache) and eng-platform (load-balancing).
eve: ops note: consider adding a canary listener rule to route 5% traffic to standby on future flaps and tighten healthcheck thresholds for this customer's pool.
oncall-sre: mitigation status: MITIGATED (traffic routed to standby). Monitoring for 2 hours, will escalate to SEV-RCA if errors persist. Closing page in 10m if stable.
alice: leaving monitoring dashboards up, will post updates if error >5% in next 15m.
ben: action items: autoscale standby pool, add healthcheck alert, run tenant isolation audit.
carla: network will run SG audit and confirm no accidental egress blocking rules exist.
dave: continuing root cause triage on cache; will propose fix (increase connection pool + circuit breaker) in follow-up.
oncall-sre: thanks everyone, good coordination. tagging incident log and adding timeline to postmortem draft. :thumbsup:
